title: Prove exact dirty-fanout tariffs over finite commutative rings
body:
## Mathematical contribution

#5089 leaves single-insertion feasibility over finite commutative rings open. This proves the exact criterion: for nonzero two-row demand `(lambda0,lambda1)`, one nonzero source insertion is possible iff the generated ideal `(lambda0,lambda1)` is principal. Either row may receive the insertion, with at most four row additions. Necessity is ideal invariance under invertible row gates; sufficiency applies the elementary finite-ring stable-reduction argument to the annihilator quotient of an ideal generator. The zero-demand exception is explicit.

Combining the criterion with Krzysztof Wójt's #5045 source-count lower bound gives an exact all-positive-price formula for every finite commutative unital ring. The predecessor's five-term envelope applies when the demand ideal is principal; the two single-insertion candidates are unavailable otherwise. Explicit restoring words attain every finite candidate. Arbitrary straight-line interleavings are covered by the lower bound.

For `R=F2[epsilon,eta]/(epsilon^2,epsilon eta,eta^2)` and demand `(epsilon,eta)`, the ideal is nonprincipal and the optimum is exactly

```text
min(mu0+mu1, 2mu0+2c1, 2mu1+2c0).
```

The three attaining count vectors are the exact Pareto frontier. At prices `(100,1000,1,1)`, the true cost is **202**; naively extending the residue-ring single-insertion term would predict **104**. This does not contradict #5089's stated residue-ring theorem.

The scope is exactly two arbitrary dirty rows and one preserved disjoint source, finite commutative R with 1 != 0, and positive stationary coefficient-independent complete abstract gate prices. Both original dirt columns return. No new supplier, native physical cost claim, kappa or selected-frontier change follows.

## Evidence and reproduction

Only five files under `research/finite-commutative-fanout/` are added: self-contained proof, exact verifier, task, provenance and replay manifest.

- Nine finite rings: 1,761 demands, including 102 nonprincipal cases; 3,522 row-specific elementary-orbit comparisons and 3,318 coefficient-selection witnesses.
- 8,601 candidate words, 51,606 forward/inverse basis checks and 3,072 literal scalar checks.
- Independent primitive-gate affine graphs with 24,576 / 5,184 / 13,824 / 960 states. Forty-five exact Dijkstra runs compare 2,348 optima, with all-state Bellman inequalities and tight descending parent paths checked.
- Eleven built-in controls and three rejected disposable optimized-script mutations: enabling unavailable single-insertion terms, dropping dirt restoration and ignoring heterogeneous prices.
- Registered warning-strict normal/optimized replay, metadata/provenance checks, committed-byte check and official export integrity pass. Read-only Git-free normal/optimized export replay produces identical output; all six exported files remain unchanged.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/finite-commutative-fanout --check-only
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/finite-commutative-fanout
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/finite-commutative-fanout
```

The universal result rests on the written proof. Finite checks are corroboration; independent human and proof-kernel acceptance are unclaimed. Full source-history ancestry checking was not run in the shallow checkout. Lean, Docker, selected supplier replay and physical caller admission were outside this algebraic contribution and were not run. All registered package commands ran.

## Open next questions

The package identifies nonsemilocal-ring elementary-orbit obstructions, three-row nonunit tariffs, and a concrete caller's complete physical price contract as distinct follow-ups, with first steps and blockers. None is claimed solved here.

## Merge Danger
